security_audit.summary: The reported command-execution and reconnaissance matches are documentation formatting and composition terminology, not executable behavior. remediation.issue: Registry downloads use a mutable raw GitHub branch URL.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the registry to an immutable release tag or commit hash, and document integrity verification before installation.

remediation.issue: Templates load JavaScript and fonts from third-party CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin dependency versions with Subresource Integrity where supported, or offer locally vendored assets for offline and controlled builds.

remediation.issue: The fallback manifest command does not verify downloaded content.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a checksum or signed release manifest and instruct users to verify it before using downloaded registry assets.

content.value_statement: Adding registry assets can require several files and composition settings. This skill guides discovery, installation, and correct wiring of blocks and components.
actual_capabilities: Lists registry blocks and components with HyperFrames catalog commands.
Explains how to install a named registry item or matching block tag.
Describes configurable block, component, and asset paths in hyperframes.json.
Shows how to wire a block into an index.html composition timeline.
Explains how to merge a component HTML, CSS, and optional script snippet.
Provides guidance for authoring and contributing a new registry item.
limitations: It does not install HyperFrames or execute commands by itself.
It does not validate the quality or security of downloaded registry assets.
It covers the documented HyperFrames registry workflow, not unrelated video tools.
Remote registry and CDN availability can affect installation and previews.

use_cases.title: Add a motion graphics block
use_cases.description: Find a block, install it, and place it on a composition timeline with the required attributes.

use_cases.title: Reuse a visual component
use_cases.description: Merge an installed effect snippet into an existing composition without missing its styles or script.

use_cases.title: Publish a registry contribution
use_cases.description: Follow the documented path from a new item idea through validation and an upstream pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Find a block
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to list HyperFrames blocks and find items tagged captions.

prompt_templates.title: Install a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install the grain-overlay component into my current HyperFrames project. Explain where the file will be placed.

prompt_templates.title: Wire a timeline block
prompt_templates.prompt: I installed data-chart. Show me how to add it to index.html at 2 seconds on track 1, including its dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a contribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new reusable HyperFrames component. Include the registry metadata, validation steps, preview expectations, and pull request preparation.

output_examples.input: How do I add a block to my composition?
output: Run the documented add command for the selected block.
Add a composition element that references the installed HTML file.
Set its composition ID, start time, duration, dimensions, and track index.

output_examples.output: Components install under compositions/components by default. The paths section in hyperframes.json can change this location.

output_examples.input: How should I discover available items?
output_examples.output: Use the catalog command with type or tag filters. Use JSON output in automated workflows, then explicitly install the chosen name.

best_practices: Use catalog JSON output in automated workflows, then install an explicitly selected item.
Review every installed HTML, CSS, and script snippet before merging it into a production composition.
Pin or verify remote registry and CDN dependencies for reproducible builds.
anti_patterns: Do not install every item from a broad tag without reviewing the expected files and dependencies.
Do not copy a component script into a composition without checking its integration notes and runtime dependencies.
Do not rely on a mutable remote registry URL for a production release without integrity controls.

faq.question: What is the difference between a block and a component?
faq.answer: A block is a standalone composition with dimensions and a timeline. A component is a reusable snippet merged into a host composition.

faq.question: Where are blocks installed by default?
faq.answer: Blocks install in the compositions directory by default.

faq.question: Where are components installed by default?
faq.answer: Components install in the compositions/components directory by default.

faq.question: Can I change installation paths?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the blocks, components, and assets paths in hyperframes.json.

faq.question: How do I find items by category?
faq.answer: Use catalog filters for item type and tag. Use JSON output when another tool must select an item.

faq.question: Should I review downloaded assets?
faq.answer: Yes. Review installed files and remote dependencies before adding them to a production composition.
